 Signal No. 2 still up over Batanes, parts of Babuyan Islands as 'Rosal' keeps strength
 Kristine Daguno-Bersamina - Philstar.com October 23, 2026 | 8:34am 
 Satellite rendering shows Typhoon Rosal (international name: Champi) taken as of 4:30 a.m. of Oct. 23, 2026. PAGASA via Facebook 
 MANILA, Philippines — Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal No. 2 remains in effect over Batanes and the northeastern portion of the Babuyan Islands as Typhoon Rosal (international name: Champi) maintained its strength while moving northwestward over the sea east-northeast of Batanes, the state weather bureau PAGASA said Friday.
 In its 5 a.m. bulletin on Friday, October 23, PAGASA said Rosal was packing maximum sustained winds of 155 kilometers per hour near the center and gusts of up to 190 kph.
 The typhoon was last spotted 275 kilometers east-northeast of Itbayat, Batanes, moving northwestward at 15 kph.
 Strong to typhoon-force winds extend up to 900 kilometers from the center.
 Warning signals 
 PAGASA raised the following tropical cyclone wind signals:
 Signal No. 2 
 Luzon 
 Batanes
 Northeastern portion of Babuyan Islands (Babuyan, Panuitan, Calayan and Camiguin islands)
 Residents in these areas may experience gale-force winds ranging from 62 to 88 kph within the next 24 hours, posing minor to moderate threats to life and property.
 Signal No. 1 
 Luzon 
 Rest of the Babuyan Islands
 Mainland Cagayan
 Northeastern portion of Isabela (Maconacon, Divilacan, Santa Maria, Cabagan, San Pablo and Palanan)
 Ilocos Norte
 Apayao
 Residents in these areas may experience strong winds ranging from 39 to 61 kph within the next 36 hours, posing minimal to minor threats to life and property.
 The northeast monsoon and Rosal's outer circulation will also bring strong to gale-force gusts over the following areas:
 Friday, October 23: Most of Luzon and the Visayas, Zamboanga del Norte, Misamis Occidental, Lanao del Norte, Camiguin, Davao Occidental and Davao Oriental.
 Saturday, October 24: Batanes, Babuyan Islands, Ilocos Norte, Polillo Islands, Bicol Region, Romblon, Capiz, Iloilo and Negros Occidental.
 Sunday, October 25: Batanes and Babuyan Islands.
 Sea conditions 
 A gale warning is in effect over the seaboards of Northern Luzon and the eastern seaboards of Central and Southern Luzon.
 Very rough to very high seas, with waves reaching up to 12 meters, are expected along the northern and eastern seaboards of Batanes.
 Waves may reach up to 9 meters along the remaining seaboards of Batanes and up to 8 meters along the northern and eastern seaboards of the Babuyan Islands and the northeastern seaboard of mainland Cagayan.
 Seas may reach up to 6 meters along the remaining seaboards of the Babuyan Islands and mainland Cagayan, the seaboard of northern Isabela and the northern seaboard of Ilocos Norte. Waves may reach up to 5.5 meters along the remaining seaboard of Isabela and up to 5 meters along the remaining seaboard of Ilocos Norte.
 Waves may reach up to 4.5 meters along the seaboards of northern Ilocos Sur and northern Aurora, the northern seaboards of Camarines Sur and Camarines Norte, and the northern and eastern seaboards of the Polillo Islands and Catanduanes.
 PAGASA warned that sea travel is risky for all types of vessels in areas where very rough to very high seas are expected. Mariners were advised to remain in port or seek shelter in a safe harbor until winds and waves subside.
 Operators of small vessels, including motorbancas, were also advised against venturing out to sea under rough conditions, especially if their vessels are ill-equipped or they lack experience.
 Track, intensity 
 Rosal is expected to continue moving generally northwestward until Saturday, October 24, before moving northward and then north-northeastward between Saturday and Sunday, October 25.
 On its forecast track, the typhoon is expected to exit the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) by early Saturday.
 PAGASA said Rosal is forecast to weaken gradually within the next 24 hours before weakening rapidly. It may be downgraded into a severe tropical storm by Saturday morning and further weaken into a tropical storm by Saturday evening.
